title: Support handoff: troubleshooting runbook, escalation paths, and known issues for Private backup/restore
creator: Talia Benson
description:
Goal
- Ensure Support + on-call SRE have a canonical, copy/paste-able troubleshooting sequence and clear escalation paths for Redwood Private backup/restore (VPC + on-prem/air-gapped).
- Reduce back-and-forth during incidents by standardizing what data to collect (logs, config, timestamps), how to interpret common failures, and when to escalate.

Scope
- Troubleshooting runbook targeted at L1/L2 Support and on-call SRE (not deep-dive engineering docs).
- Escalation paths (Support -> SRE -> Eng Private Deployments/Security/Observability).
- “Known issues” list with symptoms, quick mitigations, and tracking links.

Out of scope
- Adding new product features; this is documentation + operational process alignment.

Primary references
- Confluence: eng-sre/runbooks/private-backup-failure-troubleshooting
- Confluence: eng-private-deployments/day-2-ops/runbook-private-backup-create-and-verify
- Confluence: eng-private-deployments/day-2-ops/runbook-private-restore-in-place
- Confluence: eng-private-deployments/day-2-ops/runbook-private-restore-to-new-cluster
- Incident-bot shortcuts: /backup-status and /restore-checklist
- Support tickets: SUP-18442, SUP-18487, SUP-18511
- Internal access request pattern: INT-932 (break-glass restore role)

Deliverables
1) Canonical troubleshooting flow (L1/L2)
2) Escalation matrix + on-call checklist
3) Known issues list (with owners + tracking links)
4) Links to dashboards/alerts and where to find logs in restricted networks

Acceptance criteria
- Support can resolve the most common failures (permissions, throttling, stuck jobs, missed windows) using a single runbook without requiring Eng Private.
- Escalations include the minimum required context (cluster info, storage target, encryption mode, job logs, timestamps).
- Runbook is linked from alerts/dashboards and from incident-bot shortcuts.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Confluence runbook exists and is linked from the Private backup/restore docs + alert runbooks.
2) Escalation paths are explicit (who/when/how) and include a copy/paste checklist.
3) Known issues list covers at least: AccessDenied/KMS, backup stuck/DB contention, restore overrun, air-gapped bundle sizing, and overlapping CronJobs.
4) Support/SRE sign-off recorded in comments.
implementation_notes:
Handoff package (what we shipped)

A) Troubleshooting runbook (Support + SRE)
- Canonical doc: sources/confluence/eng-sre/runbooks/private-backup-failure-troubleshooting.json
- Intended audience:
  - L1 Support: triage + information gathering + safe customer-facing steps
  - L2 Support / on-call SRE: deeper diagnosis using dashboards/logs; coordinate restore windows

B) Escalation paths (operational)

1) L1 Support triage (customer ticket)
- Use incident-bot shortcut in the incident/customer channel:
  - /backup-status → posts: last successful backup age, recent job outcomes, dashboard links
  - /restore-checklist → posts: pre-flight checklist + links to restore runbooks
- Collect required context (paste into ticket):
  - Private deployment mode: VPC K8s | on-prem | air-gapped
  - Installer/helm chart versions (redwood-private-installer + redwood-helm-charts)
  - Storage backend: S3 | minio | NFS | other
  - Encryption mode: SSE-S3 | SSE-KMS | customer-managed KMS/HSM | local bundle
  - Error message + timestamps (UTC)
  - Backup job name + namespace + last 200 lines of logs
  - Whether a restore/upgrade/maintenance mode is in progress
- If AccessDenied / key errors: route to L2 Support/SRE immediately (usually IAM/KMS).

2) On-call SRE escalation triggers
Escalate to on-call SRE when any of the following are true:
- Backup failures for > 2 consecutive scheduled windows (or alert “Missed backup window”).
- “Last successful backup age” exceeds the customer’s stated RPO tier.
- Restore attempt has started or customer is scheduling a restore window.
- Backup job duration exceeds typical p95 by >2x (possible DB contention / storage throttling).

3) L3 engineering escalation triggers
Escalate from SRE to Eng Private Deployments (Ethan Park / Diego Santos) when:
- Reproducible failure not explained by runbook known issues.
- Evidence suggests a product bug (e.g., retention pruning deleting wrong snapshots; restore validation gate false negatives).
- Air-gapped restore fails due to format/validation mismatch.

Escalate to Security (Marcus Lin / Hanae Suzuki) when:
- Customer asks whether Redwood has access to keys/plaintext.
- KMS policy changes required that affect least-privilege or audit requirements.
- Suspected secret/cert mishandling or logs containing sensitive material.

Escalate to Observability (Allison Grant / Sergio Costa) when:
- Backup/restore dashboards missing data for a cluster or alert runbook links are wrong.
- Metric labels inconsistent with cluster identifiers or deployment mode.

C) Known issues list (tracked + customer-safe mitigations)

KI-01: S3 AccessDenied during upload (common)
- Symptoms: backup job fails quickly; logs show AccessDenied for PutObject / ListBucket; sometimes only when SSE-KMS enabled.
- Root causes:
  - Missing kms:Encrypt / kms:GenerateDataKey permissions on KMS key
  - Bucket policy denies from VPC endpoint / cross-account role mismatch
- Mitigation:
  - Validate IAM policy examples from Terraform module updates (redwood-terraform PR_318)
  - Confirm KMS key policy allows the backup role principal
- References:
  - Support ticket: SUP-18442
  - Slack thread: sources/slack/eng-infra/1732285112.json

KI-02: Backup “stuck” / runs for hours
- Symptoms: job active > 2h; high DB load; logs show slow pg_dump / lock waits.
- Root causes:
  - DB lock contention during peak traffic; insufficient resource requests; overlapping backups
- Mitigation:
  - Ensure CronJob concurrency safeguards enabled (redwood-helm-charts PR_447)
  - Move backup window off-peak; review Postgres settings guidance in runbook
- References:
  - Slack thread: sources/slack/eng-infra/1733414220.json
  - Support thread: sources/slack/support/1732981099.json

KI-03: Restore exceeds maintenance window
- Symptoms: restore completes but misses planned window; prolonged WAL replay; validation gates time out.
- Root causes:
  - Underestimated DB PITR/WAL replay time; insufficient pre-flight sizing; storage throughput
- Mitigation:
  - Run “restore plan” ahead of window; confirm artifact sizes + expected download time
  - Increase timeouts per documented values (redwood-helm-charts PR_452)
- References:
  - Support ticket: SUP-18487

KI-04: Air-gapped bundle too large for staging repo / mount
- Symptoms: on-prem operator cannot upload bundle; NFS/endpoint rejects size; transfer times impractical.
- Root causes:
  - Staging repository size constraints; lack of chunking strategy in customer environment
- Mitigation:
  - Use local mounted repository workflow; coordinate with customer storage team for temporary capacity
  - If required, split backup by retention scope (short-term workaround) and document what’s excluded
- References:
  - Support ticket: SUP-18511
  - Installer air-gapped improvements: redwood-private-installer PR_915

KI-05: Overlapping backups cause partial uploads / inconsistent state
- Symptoms: two backup jobs run simultaneously; latest snapshot incomplete; verify fails checksum.
- Root causes:
  - Cron misconfiguration; missing concurrencyPolicy/locking; manual run collided with scheduled run
- Mitigation:
  - Enforce concurrencyPolicy=Forbid and lock mechanism per Helm chart guidance (PR_447)
  - Use “backup verify” before marking snapshot as known-good

D) Where to find logs + evidence (restricted networks)
- K8s:
  - Backup job logs: kubectl -n <ns> logs job/<job-name> --tail=200
  - Events: kubectl -n <ns> describe job/<job-name>
  - Pod logs if job spawns pods: kubectl -n <ns> logs <pod>
- Product signals:
  - Maintenance mode state + write-path rejections (redwood PR_18466)
- Evidence to attach for regulated customers:
  - Backup job success timestamp, artifact checksum/verify output, retention policy, KMS key ARN (no secrets), and audit log references.

E) Dashboard + alert linkage requirements
- Ensure alerts include runbook links using the conventions from: sources/confluence/eng-platform/dashboards-and-alerts/private-backup-restore-observability.json
- Dashboards from observability-pack PR_229 + PR_237 should be the default shared links from Support macros.

F) Break-glass access pattern (Solutions/Pro Services)
- For customer-led DR drills requiring temporary privileged access (e.g., S3 restore role): follow internal helpdesk workflow INT-932.
- Requirements: manager approval + time-bounded role + audit logging enabled + ticket reference in access request.
